title: Master Sommelier Exam Advice with John Ragan, MS: Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas
why: John Ragan, MS, on the Court's own channel, framing the long road to the Master Sommelier title: no one passes it perfect and no one expects you to. Sets the tone for the whole Level 4 page.

section: The title and the way in
title: The Candidate Process with Sarafin Alvarado, MS: Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas
why: Sarafin Alvarado, MS, on what it means to be a Master Sommelier candidate and why the way in is a personal process, matching the lesson's 'apply with intent' stop.

title: The Hardest Section On The Master Sommelier Diploma Examination
why: Jarad Slipp, MS, on which of the three parts of the Master Sommelier Diploma proved hardest for him (the one he thought he was best at), a reminder that every part has to clear the bar.

title: Theory Examination: Master Sommelier Diploma Examination
why: The Court's own guide to the Theory part of the Master Sommelier Diploma: several Master Sommeliers on how they prepared for the oral exam and what the panel is listening for.

section: The clock: Theory first, then three years
title: Biggest Challenges with Kathy Morgan, MS: Courts of Master Sommeliers, Americas
why: Kathy Morgan, MS, on the fear of resetting after a Master Sommelier Diploma attempt, the lesson's 'reset' stop when the three-year window runs out.

section: Wine law: EU, US and Australia
title: TTB Boot Camp for Wineries: Labeling
why: The TTB itself walking through US wine label rules: mandatory information, appellation of origin and the COLA process, the US third of the lesson's three systems.

section: Fortified wines: Port, Sherry and Madeira
title: Master Class on 5 Fortified Wines (Port, Sherry, Madeira, Rutherglen Muscat & more)
by: THE SOUL OF WINE 와인 소울
why: A master class from two Masters of Wine on five fortified wines, including Port, Sherry and Madeira: how and when the spirit goes in, and the styles that result.

title: WSET 3 Minute Spirit School - Whisky, presented by Richard Paterson
why: WSET's 3 Minute Spirit School on whisky with master blender Richard Paterson: an overview from production to blending to tasting, one worked example of how base, still and wood shape a spirit.

section: Beer, cider and keeping it all in condition
title: Four Tips for Preserving Beer Quality At Retail
why: The Brewers Association's four tips for keeping beer in good condition after it leaves the brewery, the lesson's 'keeping it right' stop. Covers beer only, not cider.

title: Tasting Examination Advice with Christopher Bates, MS: Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas
why: Christopher Bates, MS, on what to take into account when preparing for the blind tasting part of the Master Sommelier Diploma, the same grid at a higher bar.

title: Tasting Group Advice with Shayn Bjornholm, MS: Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas
why: Shayn Bjornholm, MS, the Court's examination director, on why the people in a tasting group need to be on the same path, the lesson's point about calibrating the method together.

title: The Secret to Wine Vintages
why: Wine Folly compares two vintages of the same López de Heredia Crianza to show how the year changes the wine, the skill behind pinning a vintage blind.

title: Learn to blind taste like a Master Sommelier:  Wine Study Hall from SOMM TV
why: Jill Zimorski, MS, on the fundamentals of blind tasting and what trips tasters up, which comes down to knowing the benchmark (classic) examples well enough to spot them.

section: Aperitifs and the start of the meal
title: Guide to Aperitifs | How to Drink
why: How To Drink tours the aperitif category, tasting a cross-section of bottles with their history, the 'know the product' stop for the start of the meal.

section: Glassware for every drink and every room
title: Wine Glasses: Science or Scam? (The Riedel Story)
why: Wine Folly on the Riedel story and whether glass shape really changes what's in it, the thinking behind picking the right glass for each drink.

title: Inside Hennessy | How Cognac is Made?
why: Julien Miquel inside Hennessy's distillery: how Cognac is distilled from wine and aged in French oak, the brandy knowledge behind recommending and pouring it.

title: Wine Protips: How To Tell If Your Wine is Corked
why: Patrick Cappiello, a New York wine director, explains cork taint and how to tell a corked bottle, the knowledge behind handling a rejected bottle with the guest.

title: Sommelier Profile: Eric Zillier l Wine Spectator
why: Wine Spectator profiles Eric Zillier of Alto in New York, a Grand Award list, on the qualities that make a great wine list.

title: Why Wine is So Expensive at Restaurants | World Of Wine | Bon Appétit
why: Sommelier André Hueston Mack walks step by step through how he designs and prices a restaurant wine list, and why bottles cost what they do.

title: Three Tier System Of Alcohol Beverage Businesses
why: Beverage Trade Network on the three-tier system that every bottle passes through: importer or supplier, distributor, then the restaurant or retailer.

section: The cellar: storage, inventory and turnover
title: A Sommelier Shows His Wine Inventory Room: Thomas Brenner
why: Sommelier and wine buyer Thomas Brenner shows his club's wine inventory room and explains how the bottles are placed and stored.

title: What Is The Role Of a Head Sommelier?: Lindsey Young
why: Lindsey Young on the role of a head sommelier, the person on staff who knows the wine inside out and carries the program, which includes teaching the team.

title: Getting Started With CMS-A With Robert Jones, MS: Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas
why: Robert Jones, MS, on the one line of encouragement from a mentor that started his path through the Court's levels to Master Sommelier.

title: A New Online Course From The Court of Master Sommeliers, Americas: SommBIZ
why: The Court's own introduction to SommBIZ, its course in beverage business fundamentals and financial management for sommeliers who run a program.
